hero.h1: Sewer Cleaning and Rodding in Evanston, IL
hero.sub: Water rising at the basement floor drain or every drain slowing at once means the main line is blocked. We rod it clear to the city sewer and show you the cause on camera. Our Evanston office is on Orrington Avenue, downtown.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber feeding the cable from a drum rodding machine into an outdoor sewer cleanout in a front yard

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: What We Pull Out of Evanston Sewer Lines
blocks.intro: Most clogs here come from the age of the pipe and the trees above it.

items.body: Fine roots fill old clay joints and catch paper.
Even flushable wipes snag on roots.
Roots back in months? [Hydro jetting](/evanston/hydro-jetting) or a [repair](/evanston/sewer-repair) lasts longer.

blocks.intro: Clear it, see it, explain it.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.h2: Why Evanston Sewer Clogs Peak in Spring
blocks.body: Tree roots grow fastest when the ground thaws and the trees leaf out. In an old clay lateral, that's when fine roots push through the joints and fill the pipe. Add a few heavy spring rains and a full combined sewer, and a partly blocked line gives up. That's why many Evanston homeowners with a root history book their rodding in late winter. It clears the line just before the growth season starts.

blocks.h2: Sewer Cleaning Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: How often should my Evanston sewer be rodded?
items.preview: Yearly if roots are a problem.
items.answer: If roots have blocked it before, plan on once a year, ideally late winter.

items.q: What's the difference between rodding and jetting?
items.preview: Rodding cuts a path. Jetting cleans the walls.
items.answer: Rodding cuts through roots and clogs. Jetting uses high-pressure water to scour the whole pipe wall, so it usually lasts longer.

items.q: Is the backup the city's problem or mine?
items.preview: On a dry day, it's usually your lateral.
items.answer: If it happens without rain, the blockage is usually in your lateral. During heavy storms, the combined sewer can back up too.
We can usually get in without one, but adding an outside cleanout makes every future visit faster.

items.preview: It can slow regrowth, not clear a clog.
items.answer: Root treatments can slow regrowth after a cleaning, but they won't open a blocked line. Mechanical cleaning comes first.

items.q: How much does sewer cleaning cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access, the length of the line and the blockage. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
